answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable deposit before it can submit jobs, and the protocol slashes that deposit when independent audits confirm fabricated work. A Sybil attacker can mint identities cheaply, but every identity needs its own locked capital and risks losing it, so multiplying agents raises the attacker’s cost in proportion to the influence they seek. The tundra, pigment, and sable markets can share this rule without treating names or appearances as proof of personhood.
